input: Contact HR about unused vacation days expiring

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing how many days are expiring and by when determines how urgent and specific the message needs to be.
Whether the user is contacting HR on their own behalf or on behalf of someone else (e.g., a team) changes the framing and tone entirely.
The expiration deadline dictates urgency and whether this needs to happen today or can be planned over days.
Company policies may limit options — knowing if there are rules about carryover, payout, or extension shapes what the user can actually ask for.
The desired outcome (extend the days, get a payout, schedule time off) completely changes what the user should say to HR.
The channel — email, phone call, HR portal, in-person — determines the format of the output needed.
Understanding what a successful interaction looks like (a written confirmation, a policy exception, a booked holiday) defines when this task is truly done.

gold.taskTitle: Contact HR about expiring unused vacation days
gold.taskDescription: The user needs to reach out to their HR department to address unused vacation days that are at risk of expiring.

questions.title: How many vacation days are at risk of expiring?
questions.description: Establish the exact number of unused days in question so the message can reference specifics.

questions.title: Are you contacting HR for yourself or someone else?
questions.description: Determine whether this is a personal inquiry or being handled on behalf of a colleague or team.

questions.title: When exactly do the vacation days expire?
questions.description: Pinpoint the expiration date to set the urgency level and deadline for the outreach.

questions.title: What outcome do you want from HR — extension, payout, or something else?
questions.description: Clarify the specific ask so the communication is targeted and actionable.

questions.title: Do you know your company's policy on vacation day carryover or expiry?
questions.description: Understanding existing policy constraints shapes what can realistically be requested.

questions.title: How do you plan to contact HR — email, call, or HR portal?
questions.description: The chosen channel determines whether the output needed is a written draft, talking points, or a form.

questions.title: What would a successful response from HR look like to you?
questions.description: Define the end state so the task has a clear completion condition — e.g., written confirmation, approved time off, or a policy exception granted.
